html:
A Tatar Muslim state on the middle Volga with its capital at Kazan, from about 1438 to 1552. It held the lands of the old Volga Bulgars, and the map shows it in 1530 reaching east toward the Urals.

It was one of the successor states of the Golden Horde, founded by the exiled khan Ulugh Muhammad. Its people were Tatars, Chuvash, Mari, Udmurts and Bashkirs, and Kazan grew rich on Volga trade in furs, grain and slaves. For a century it raided Russian lands and fought Moscow, which tried to place friendly khans on its throne.

In 1552 Ivan the Terrible took Kazan after a long siege and celebrated with Saint Basil's Cathedral in Moscow. Astrakhan fell four years later. With the whole Volga in Russian hands, the Tsardom of Muscovy became an empire of many peoples, and the way lay open to the Khanate of Sibir and Siberia beyond. Kazan is now the capital of Tatarstan.
